newsitem.title: USA: Alex. Brown, Bankers Trust muni effect uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Alex. Brown, Bankers Trust muni effect uncertain.

text.p: It's too early to tell how the proposed Alex. Brown Inc. and Bankers Trust New York Corp merger will affect municipal professionals there specifically, but a Bankers Trust spokeman said the two firms have little overlap in general.

Bankers Trust through BT Securities Corp has focused on municipal derivatives and short-term finance, sales, trading and marketing out to 10 years. Alex. Brown through Alex. Brown & Sons Inc has focused on traditional municipal underwriting and sales.

"Unlike some commercial banking mergers that we have seen recently where there is a lot of overlap and the intent is to put them together and to squeeze out a lot of expense, this isn't one of those kinds," Tom Parisi, a Banker Trust spokesman, said. "This is one where the firms are complementary, where they have strengths that we don't and would take a long time to build."
Alex. Brown has strength in equity and equity research, while Bankers Trust has debt side strength, particularly in high-yield debt and structured finance, Parisi said.

Baltimore-based Alex. Brown has 56 municipal professionals and 17 assistants spread through the offices of Alex. Brown & Sons in Baltimore, Boston, New York and San Francisco, Greg Conderacci, a spokesman, said.
Thirty-two professionals are in sales and trading, 20 in public finance and four on the variable rate desk, he said.
Conderacci was unable to say how the merger would affect municipal professionals.
"The merger has just been announced, so we have not worked out the details of how we are going forward in the municipal bond area," he said. "This is new to everybody here."
According to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group, Alex. Brown is senior manager on no major new issues this week.
Back in August, Alex. Brown & Sons named former Prudential Securities Inc head trader Gerard McNamara principal and head of municipal bond trading.
Then, in September, Alex. Brown tapped former Greenwich Partners Inc vice president John Wasilewski as its new institutional municipal sales manager.
At the time, C. Randall Coleman, manager of Alex. Brown's municipal department, said the hirings represented the firm's drive to build its secondary market institutional business.
Coleman could not be reached for comment Monday.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, Alex. Brown & Sons Inc ranked 64th among municipal bond underwriters when full credit was given to the book manager. The firm managed 16 offerings totaling $353.6 million for a 0.2 percent market share.
However, the firm improved its rank to 53rd for the period from Jan. 1, 1997 to April 1, 1997, when it managed four deals totaling $84 million for a 0.2 percent market share.
For the same period in 1996, Alex Brown ranked 85th after managing two deals totaling $46.4 million for a 0.1 percent market share.
For it's part, Bankers Trust currently employs between 15 and 20 professionals in its municipal department, spokesman Parisi said.
Donna Garban, a managing director who runs BT's municipal business, said the firm is involved in derivatives and short-term finance, sales, trading and marketing out to 10 years.
BT does underwriting, but it is limited primarily to short-term notes, she said.

So far this quarter BT has underwritten $213 million in short-term notes. For full year 1996, the firm was ranked third in that category with more than $1 billion in competitive note underwritings. The ranking was from Securities Data Co, and gave full credit to lead managers, she said.

"Our main core business is variable rate remarketing," Garban said. "It's a business we've been in since the invention of variable rates in the early '80s. We are top ranked in both weekly remarketing as well as synthetic remarketing, which is derivatives." Those rankings were from sources other than SDC, she said.
The firm elected to focus on short-term securities and derivatives back in the early 1990s, Garban said.
((--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655))
